doc.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022

title: End of tours and Mick Jagger's fitness at nearly 80
summary: Ries treats each tour as possibly the last, praises Mick's discipline, and thinks the band is better now.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: When one of the tours ends do you speculate on will they do this again? They keep doing it again, don’t they?

But I really look at the end of every tour that that’s the last one because I can’t — first of all they’re almost 80 — Charlie unfortunately died at 80. Mick’s, they’re turning 79 this year. So it’s kind of and it’s their 60th anniversary tour. 60 years of doing this. So it’s like incredible, and you know going back to the surprises, Mick of course — you see a guy that’s that age running around stage and you think how does he do it? Well because he eats right, he has a trainer on the road, he exercises, he’s in incredible shape. So it’s kind of almost like an inspiration realizing hey you know you’re approaching 80 you don’t have to sit in the chair in the corner of your room and just read a book and be feeble. I mean you can be active and moving, and he’s proof of that. I mean he takes care of himself and he’s really diligent about being careful with his body and taking care, and he practices, he took voice lessons even in his late 60s or whatever, he started getting a vocal
coach because you realize hey, to keep this together warming up and all of that — so he really is like dedicated to — I think they’re better now than they were in a way.
